sophia: Heads up — ran the HF->Redwood conversion for the new spm model and hit a weird token remap that breaks chat templates.
aj: ugh, details? what specifically is broken?
marc: quick guess: special tokens mapping or vocab_size mismatch during merges.
sophia: Exactly that. The model was trained with SentencePiece and we used the standard spm_to_bpe conversion script. After conversion some special tokens end up with new ids that collide with subword ids. Example from local inspect: `'<|system|>' -> 50260` but after merges the tokenizer thinks 50260 is a regular token that maps to 'Ġthe' (or similar).
aj: Do you have the config.json and the merges/vocab snippet?
sophia: Pasting small bits — truncated for thread: ```
# config.json excerpt
{"model_type": "gpt2", "vocab_size": 50261, "bos_token_id": 50256, "eos_token_id": 50257, "unk_token_id": 50258, "additional_special_tokens": ["<|system|>", "<|assistant|>"]}
```
and merges (top 3 lines): ```
Ġt h
Ġth e
a s
```
marc: That vocab_size looks off by a few vs the actual spm vocab (we saw +3 extras). Those off-by-Ns shift all special token ids if the conversion appends special tokens after building the BPE vocab.
aj: Right — our conversion pipeline appends additional_special_tokens at the end of the token->id map. If the SentencePiece mapping has a different ordering, indexes shift.
sophia: The real kicker: SentencePiece normalization removed some zero-width joiners and combined certain whitespace tokens, so the produced token strings differ. That caused a different merge order and the merges.txt produced by the converter is incompatible with the original training-time merges.
marc: Does the model metadata include the original "sp_model_args" or a merges provenance field? If not it's hard to ensure deterministic mapping.
sophia: No provenance. We only had the .model file and tokenizer.json. CI run shows perplexity jump on small evals after conversion (~+6 ppl).
aj: Could be that some frequent special token (system/assistant) got reassigned to a subword and now the model sees a different token at runtime — huge regression for chat templates.
marc: Short-term mitigation: remap special tokens to reserved low ids (0..N) and update config.json to reflect explicit token ids instead of relying on append-order. That keeps them stable across conversions.
sophia: Tried that locally: remapped special tokens to 1..3 and patched the tokenizer.json. It fixed the chat template parsing, but downstream model weights expect embeddings in their original positions — so you need to reorder embedding matrix or create an id->id mapping layer at serve time.
aj: Embedding remap is doable in a conversion step: emit a permute_embeddings.py that reads model.bin and reorders according to new tokenizer.ids_to_tokens. But that's invasive for on-the-fly Dedicated conversions.
marc: Another approach: preserve original SentencePiece ids by translating spm ids -> target BPE ids using a stable bijection produced from the spm tokenizer object (not from merges file). Basically: for each spm piece map the string -> desired bpe id and write that mapping explicitly into tokenizer.json. That avoids relying on merge ordering.
sophia: Good idea. I hacked a script that iterates spm.vocab() and writes explicit token->id pairs. It reduced ppl delta to ~+0.5 on the smoke eval. Still need to run larger eval.
aj: Also ensure normalizer config matches (NFKC, nfkc_cf, unicode normalization). Mismatched normalizer between training and runtime can produce tokenization differences even with identical vocab.
marc: For quant experiments: watch out if you quantize embedding rows in a different order than the token->id map — quant artifacts will show as weird token-level regressions.
sophia: Filed a short RFC: add "token_provenance": {"source":"spm","source_vocab_size":"50258","normalizer":"nfkc"} into our conversion metadata and include explicit token id mapping file. Will post PR.
aj: +1 on the RFC. Also add an automated check in CI: compare top-10k most frequent tokens' mappings pre/post conversion and fail if >0.1% mismatch.
ci-bot: conversion-pipeline/job#342 completed — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-internal/conversions/1772005123/
marc: Thanks — can you attach the mapping JSON from the artifacts to this thread?
sophia: I uploaded mapping.json and a short smoke eval summary to the CI artifacts. Linking: https://s3.redwood/internal/conversions/1772005123/mapping.json
aj: Great, I'll run full eval and try the permute_embeddings approach on a duplicated model. Will report back. :thumbsup:
